title: Napoleon Bonaparte (1769–1821) — Artillery Outsider, Austerlitz, Overreach, and St. Helena

teenKit.tldr: A starving, broke 26-year-old artillery dropout goes from pawning his watch for dinner to seizing absolute control of a collapsing government using sheer audacity and stolen cannons.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It proves that in moments of total systemic collapse, absolute confidence and ruthless execution can turn a complete nobody into the master of the room.
keyTakeaways: Desperation can breed hyper-focused risk-taking when an outsider is suddenly handed the keys to the kingdom.
Controlling critical infrastructure—like sprinting across Paris to steal 40 brass cannons before your enemy gets them—wins conflicts before they even start.
Power often flows to the person willing to make an uncompromising ultimatum when everyone else is panicking.

vocab.meaning: Heavy military weaponry like cannons and large-scale projectile launchers designed to blast through fortifications and crowds.
A political rebel or insurgent who fought to overthrow the new French Republic and restore the absolute monarchy and king to power.
A professional soldier hired to fight for a foreign country or faction purely for money rather than patriotic loyalty.
A willingness to take shockingly bold, high-stakes risks that ordinary people would consider completely reckless.

quiz.question: What was Napoleon's physical and financial state right before he was summoned to command Paris?
options: He was a celebrated war hero living in a luxury mansion near the Tuileries.
He was a starving, broke unemployed officer who had to pawn his watch just to buy dinner.
He was an active-duty general leading 30,000 troops against the royalist rebels.
He had already packed his bags to move to the Ottoman Empire and become a merchant.
quiz.explanation: Napoleon was completely destitute, walking the cold streets of Paris with scuffed-through boots and no command.

quiz.question: How did Joachim Murat secure the 40 brass cannons for Napoleon?
options: He bought them legally from a corrupt weapons dealer using stolen government funds.
He negotiated a treaty with the royalist mob to split the artillery evenly.
He galloped five miles to a military camp and beat the enemy to the cannons by mere minutes.
He built them from scratch overnight using scrap metal found in the Tuileries Palace.
quiz.explanation: Murat rode hard to the Sublons camp, cutting down anyone in his path to snatch the artillery right before the mob arrived.

quiz.question: What psychological tactic did Napoleon use when the terrified government offered him supreme military command?
options: He immediately burst into tears of gratitude and swore eternal loyalty.
He demanded a massive cash advance and a written guarantee of future promotions.
He stood completely motionless for three minutes before giving an uncompromising ultimatum.
He rejected the offer outright and tried to flee the country to avoid the chaos.
quiz.explanation: He held total silence to establish dominance, then stated that once his sword was drawn, he wouldn't sheath it until order was restored.
